page: Microsoft Azure E96nds_v6 is a memory-optimized instance operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine is built on the x86_64 Intel architecture and provides 96 dedicated vCPUs paired with 768 GB of total system RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration via discrete GPUs is not present in this configuration.

Storage capabilities include 5669 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The instance family incorporates network optimization for high throughput and reduced latency. Public networking requires explicit assignment, as zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned with the instance.

Resource distribution emphasizes substantial memory capacity coupled directly with expansive, low-latency NVMe scratch space. This design avoids external storage latency for temporary datasets and caching layers. The configuration is aligned with enterprise workloads requiring dense in-memory processing, such as large relational databases, in-memory key-value stores, distributed analytics nodes, and high-capacity transactional engines.
description: Microsoft Azure E96nds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel processor and managed through Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 96 dedicated vCPUs and 768 GB of RAM, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided through a high-capacity 5669 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by support for Premium Storage tiers. The instance is network-optimized and lacks dedicated GPU accelerators. In terms of resource efficiency, the instance aggregates large amounts of memory and local low-latency storage into a single host footprint, mitigating the network overhead associated with detached block volumes for ephemeral data. Consequently, the hardware configuration is designed for large-scale relational databases, distributed in-memory data grids, enterprise resource planning engines, and intensive analytics pipelines requiring substantial memory capacity and high-throughput local scratch space.
